Then went he out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.<div eID="gen4052" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4053" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">33. </hi>Et venit Laban in tabernaculum Iahacob, et in tabernaculum Leah, et in tabernaculum ambarum ancillarum, et non invenit: et egressus de tabernaculo Lea, venit in tabernaculum Rachel.<div eID="gen4053" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4054" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">34.</hi> Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel’s furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found <hi type="italic">them</hi> not.<div eID="gen4054" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4055" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">34. </hi>Rachel autem acceperat idola, et posuerat ea in clitellis cameli, et sedebat super ea: et contrectavit Laban totum tabernaculum, et non invenit.<div eID="gen4055" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4056" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">35. </hi>And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women <hi type="italic">is</hi> upon me. And he searched, but found not the images.<div eID="gen4056" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4057" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">35. </hi>Et dixit ad patrem suum, Ne sit ira in oculis domini mei, quod non possim surgere a facie tua: quia consuetudo mulierum est mihi: et scrutatus est, et non invenit idola.<div eID="gen4057" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4058" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">36. </hi>And Jacob was wroth, and chode with Laban: and Jacob answered and said to Laban, What <hi type="italic">is</hi> my trespass? what <hi type="italic">is</hi> my sin, that thou hast so hotly pursued after me?<div eID="gen4058" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4059" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">36. </hi>Tunc iratus est Iahacob, et jurgatus est cum Laban: et respondit Iahacob, et dixit ad Laban, Quae est praevaricatio mea, quod peccatum meum, quod persecutus es me?<div eID="gen4059" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4060" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">37. </hi>Whereas thou hast searched all my stuff, what hast thou found of all thy household stuff? set <hi type="italic">it</hi> here before my brethren and thy brethren, that they may judge betwixt us both.<div eID="gen4060" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4061" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">37. </hi>Quando contrectasti omnem supellectilem meam, quid invenistiex omni supellectili domus tuae? pone hic coram fratribus meis et fratribus tuis, et declarent inter nos ambos.<div eID="gen4061" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4062" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">38. </hi>This twenty years <hi type="italic">have</hi> I <hi type="italic">been</hi> with thee; thy ewes and thy she goats have not cast their young, and the rams of thy flock have I not eaten.<div eID="gen4062" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4063" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">38. </hi>Iam viginti annos fui tecum; oves tuae et caprae non abortiverunt: et arietes pecudum tuarum non comedi.<div eID="gen4063" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4064" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">39. </hi>That which was torn <hi type="italic">of beasts</hi> I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it; of my hand didst thou require it, <hi type="italic">whether</hi> stolen by day, or stolen by night.<div eID="gen4064" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4065" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">39. </hi>Raptum non attuli tibi, ego poenas luebam pro eo: de manu mea requirebas illud, quod furto ablatum erat tam die quam nocte.<div eID="gen4065" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4066" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">40. </hi><hi type="italic">Thus</hi> I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from mine eyes.<div eID="gen4066" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4067" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">40. </hi>Ita fui ut interdiu consumeret me aestus, et gelu in nocte, et recedebat somnus meus ab oculis meis.<div eID="gen4067" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4068" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">41. </hi>Thus have I been twenty years in thy house; I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle: and thou hast changed my wages ten times.<div eID="gen4068" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4069" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">41. </hi>Iam mihi sunt viginti anni in domo tua: servivi tibi quatuordecim annos pro duabus filiabus tuis, et sex annos pro pecudibus tuis, et mutasti mercedem meam decem vicibus.<div eID="gen4069" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4070" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">42. </hi>Except the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely thou hadst sent me away now empty. God hath seen mine affliction and the labour of my hands, and rebuked <hi type="italic">thee</hi> yesternight.<div eID="gen4070" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4071" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">42. </hi>Nisi Deus patris mei, Deus Abraham, et pavor Ishac fuisset pro me, certe nunc vacuum dimisisses me: afflictionem meam et laborem manuum mearum vidit Deus, et increpavit to nocte praeterita.<div eID="gen4071" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4072" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">43. </hi>And Laban answered and said unto Jacob, <hi type="italic">These</hi> daughters <hi type="italic">are</hi> my daughters, and <hi type="italic">these</hi> children <hi type="italic">are</hi> my children, and <hi type="italic">these</hi> cattle <hi type="italic">are</hi> my cattle, and all that thou seest <hi type="italic">is</hi> mine: and what can I do this day unto these my daughters, or unto their children which they have born?<div eID="gen4072" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4073" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">43. </hi>Tunc respondit Laban, et dixit ad Iahacob, Filiae, filiae meae sunt: et filii, filii mei sunt: et pecudes meae sunt: et quicquid vides, meum est: et filiabus meis quid faciam istis hodie, vel filiis earum quos pepererunt?<div eID="gen4073" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4074" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">44. </hi>Now therefore come thou, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a witness between me and thee.<div eID="gen4074" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4075" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">44. </hi>Et nunc, veni, percutiamus foedus ego et tu, et erit in testimonium inter me et inter to.<div eID="gen4075" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4076" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">45. </hi>And Jacob took a stone, and set it up <hi type="italic">for</hi> a pillar.<div eID="gen4076" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4077" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">45. </hi>Tulit itaque Iahacob lapidem, et erexit illum in statuam.<div eID="gen4077" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4078" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">46. </hi>And Jacob said unto his brethren, Gather stones; and they took stones, and made an heap: and they did eat there upon the heap.<div eID="gen4078" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4079" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">46. </hi>Et dixit Iahacob fratribus suis, Colligite lapides: et tulerunt lapides, et fecerunt cumulum, et comederunt ibi super cumulum.<div eID="gen4079" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4080" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">47. </hi>And Laban called it Jegarsahadutha: but Jacob called it Galeed.<div eID="gen4080" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4081" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">47. </hi>Et vocavit eum Laban Jegar Sahadutha: Iahacob autem vocavit eum Galhed.<div eID="gen4081" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4082" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">48. </hi>And Laban said, This heap <hi type="italic">is</hi> a witness between me and thee this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed;<div eID="gen4082" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4083" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">48. </hi>Et dixit Laban, Cumulus iste sit testis inter me et to hodie. Idcirco vocavit nomen ejus Galhed,<div eID="gen4083" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4084" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">49. </hi>And Mizpah; for he said, The LORD watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.<div eID="gen4084" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4085" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">49. </hi>Et Mispah: quia dixit, Speculetur Iehova inter me et to, quando latebimus alter alterum.<div eID="gen4085" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4086" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">50. </hi>If thou shalt afflict my daughters, or if thou shalt take <hi type="italic">other</hi> wives beside my daughters, no man <hi type="italic">is</hi> with us; see, God <hi type="italic">is</hi> witness betwixt me and thee.<div eID="gen4086" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4087" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">50. </hi>Si afflixeris filias meas, et si acceperis uxores super filias meas, non est quisquam nobiscum, vide, Deus est testis inter me et to.<div eID="gen4087" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4088" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">51.</hi> And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and behold <hi type="italic">this</hi> pillar, which I have cast betwixt me and thee;<div eID="gen4088" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4089" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">51.</hi> Dixit ergo Laban ad Iahacob, Ecce, cumulus iste, et ecce statua, quam jeci inter me et to.<div eID="gen4089" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4090" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">52. </hi>This heap <hi type="italic">be</hi> witness, and <hi type="italic">this</hi> pillar <hi type="italic">be</hi> witness, that I will not pass over this heap to thee, and that thou shalt not pass over this heap and this pillar unto me, for harm.<div eID="gen4090" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4091" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">52. </hi>Testis cumulus iste, et testis statua, quod ego non transibo veniens ad to cumulum istum, et statuam istam, ad malum.<div eID="gen4091" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4092" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">53. </hi>The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge betwixt us. And Jacob sware by the fear of his father Isaac.<div eID="gen4092" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4093" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">53. </hi>Deus Abraham et Deus Nachor judicet inter nos, Deus patris eorum: et juravit Iahacob per pavorem patris sui Ishac.<div eID="gen4093" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4094" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">54. </hi>Then Jacob offered sacrifice upon the mount, and called his brethren to eat bread: and they did eat bread, and tarried all night in the mount.<div eID="gen4094" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4095" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">54. </hi>Et mactavit Iahacob victimam in monte, et vocavit fratres suos, ut comederent panem: et comederunt panem, et pernoctaverunt in monte.<div eID="gen4095" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen4096" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">55.</hi> And early in the morning Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them: and Laban departed, and returned unto his place.<div eID="gen4096" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen4097" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">55.</hi> Et surrexit Laban mane, et osculatus est filios suos ac filias suas, benedixitque eis, et abiit: et reversus est Laban ad locum suum.<div eID="gen4097" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row> </table> <div sID="gen4098" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen4098" type="x-p"/>

entries.b70e4004a722cf4fe8f7a86eaf3231b5348f03c1:
<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="30" type="chapter">
                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXX.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1 AND when Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envyed her sister, and said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">A speech full of impatience and bordering upon blasphe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />my, and striking at God himself through <ns0:hi>Iacobs</ns0:hi> sides. For which therefore she afterwards smarted, dying by that very means whereby she hoped to prevent her death and prolong her life, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 35. 18.</ns0:note>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 And Jacobs anger was kindled against Ra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chel <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">For the injury done to himself and especially for the sin against God, in which case anger is not onely lawfull but neces<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sary.</ns0:note>, and he said, am I in Gods stead <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">It is Gods prerogative to give Children. See <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 16. 2. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 2. 5, 6. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 113. 9. and 127. 3.</ns0:note>, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 And she said, Behold my maid Bilhah: go in unto her, and she shall bear upon my knees <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">An Ellipsis or short speech, she shall bear a child which may be laid <ns0:hi>upon my knees</ns0:hi> or in my lap, which I may adopt and bring up as if it were my own. See <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 50. 23. <ns0:hi>Is<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi> 66. 12.</ns0:note>, that I may also <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> be built by her.</ns0:note> have children by her <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">For as servants, so their work and fruit, were not their own, but their masters.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid to wife: and Jacob went in unto her.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And Bilhah conceived, and bare Jacob a son.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And Rachel said, God hath judged me <ns0:note n="*" place="bottom">Pleaded my cause or given sentence for me, as this phrase is oft taken.</ns0:note>, and
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:30" />
hath also heard my voice, and hath given me a son; therefore called she his name <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, <ns0:hi>judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> Dan.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 And Bilhah Rachels maid conceived again, and bare Jacob a second son.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And Rachel said, with <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> wra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stlings of God.</ns0:note> great wrastlings <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>With wrastlings of God,</ns0:hi> either with great and hard wrastlings or strivings; or by wrastling with God in fervent prayer, and by Gods grace and strength.</ns0:note>, have I wrastled with my sister, and I have prevail<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Which was not true; for her sister exceeded her both in the number of her Children, and in her propriety in them, being the fruit of her own womb, not of her handmaids, as <ns0:hi>Rachels</ns0:hi> were. Here is an instance how partial Judges most persons are in their own causes and concernments.</ns0:note>; and she called his name <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, <ns0:hi>my wrastling.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Called Matt. 4. 13. <ns0:hi>Nephtha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lian.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> Naphtali.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 When Leah saw that she had left bearing, she took Zilpah her maid, and gave her Jacob to wife.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 And Zilpah Leahs maid bare Jacob a son.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 And Leah said, A troop cometh <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>Good luck cometh,</ns0:hi> my design hath well succeeded: an happy star hath shone upon me; and such a star in the opi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nion of Astrologers is that of <ns0:hi>Iupiter,</ns0:hi> which by the <ns0:hi>Arabians</ns0:hi> is called <ns0:hi>Gad.</ns0:hi> This may well agree to <ns0:hi>Leah</ns0:hi> and her heathenish Education, and the manners of the <ns0:hi>Chaldaeans</ns0:hi> who were much given to the study of the stars.</ns0:note>: And she called his name <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, <ns0:hi>a troop or company.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> Gad.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And Zilpah Leahs maid bare Jacob a second son.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And Leah said, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> in my happiness.</ns0:note> Happy am I, for the daugh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters <ns0:note n="†" place="bottom">Of Men, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Women, as <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 31. 29. <ns0:hi>Cant.</ns0:hi> 6. 9.</ns0:note>, will call me blessed: and she called his name <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, <ns0:hi>happy.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> Asher.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found Mandrakes <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The word is onely found here and <ns0:hi>Cant.</ns0:hi> 7. 13. whence it appears that it is a Plant or Fruit of pleasant smell, such as the Mandrake is said to be by <ns0:hi>Dioscorides</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Levinus Lemnius,</ns0:hi> and by St. <ns0:hi>Austin</ns0:hi> upon his own experience. If it be said, this was too early for Mandrakes to be ripe, it being now but wheat harvest, it may be replyed, that fruits ripen much sooner in those hot Countries, than elsewhere, and that they are not here said to be ripe, but onely to be gathered.</ns0:note> in the field, and brought them unto his mother Leah. Then Ra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chel said to Leah, Give me I pray thee of thy sons Mandrakes <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Which she might desire either because they were pleasant to the eye or tast, or because they were thought helpful to conception.</ns0:note>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And she said unto her, Is it a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and wouldst thou take away my sons Mandrakes also? and Ra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chel said, Therefore he shall lie with thee to night <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> either did equally divide the times between his two Wives; or rather had more estranged himself from <ns0:hi>Leah,</ns0:hi> and cohabited principally with <ns0:hi>Rachel;</ns0:hi> which occasioned the foregoing expostulation.</ns0:note>, for thy sons Mandrakes.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 And Jacob came out of the field in the even<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in unto me: for surely I have hired thee with my sons Mandrakes. And he lay with her that night <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">He ratified their agreement that he might preserve peace and love amongst them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 And God hearkned unto Leah <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Notwithstanding her many infirmities. Hence it appears, that she was moved herein not by any inordinate lust but by a desire of Children.</ns0:note>, and she conceived, and bare Jacob the fifth son.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 And Leah said, God hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Thus she mistakes the answer of her prayers for a recom<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pence of her errour.</ns0:note>: and she called his name <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, <ns0:hi>an hire.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> Issachar.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 And Leah conceived again, and bare Jacob the sixth son.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 And Leah said, God hath endued me with a good dowry: now will my husband dwell with me, because I have born him six sons: and she called his name <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, <ns0:hi>dwel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">called Matt. 4. 13. <ns0:hi>Zibulon.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> Zebulun.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And afterwards she bare a daughter, and cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led her name <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, <ns0:hi>judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> Dinah.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 And God remembred Rachel, and God hearkned to her, and opened her womb.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 And she conceived and bare a son, and said, God hath taken away my reproach <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Barrenness was then accounted a great reproach, especially in that race, because it was a kind of curse, whereby such per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons were excluded both from the first and general blessing of fructification given to all mankind, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 1. 28. and from the special blessing given to <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> for the multiplication of his feed; and from all hopes of being the progenitors of the bles<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed <ns0:hi>Messias.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">24 And she called his name <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, <ns0:hi>ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> Joseph, and said, The LORD shall add to me another son.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="25">25 And it came to pass, when Rachel had born Joseph, that Jacob said unto Laban, send me away, that I may go unto mine own place, and to my country <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Canaan,</ns0:hi> which he calleth <ns0:hi>his Country</ns0:hi> in regard both of his former and long habitation in it, and of the right which he had to it by Gods promise. See <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 28. 13.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="26">26 Give <ns0:hi>me</ns0:hi> my wives and my children, for whom I have served thee, and let me go, for thou knowest my service which I have done thee.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="27">27 And Laban said unto him, I pray thee, if I have <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 39. 21.</ns0:note> found favour in thine eyes, <ns0:hi>tarry:</ns0:hi> for I have learned by experience, that the LORD hath blessed me for thy sake.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="28">28 And he said, Appoint me thy wages, and I will give it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="29">29 And he said unto him, Thou knowest how I have served thee, and how thy cattle was with me <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">How carefully it was managed, and how greatly improved by my care and industry.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="30">30 For it was little which thou hadst before I <ns0:hi>came</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Comparatively to what now it is.</ns0:note>, and it is <ns0:hi>now</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> broken forth.</ns0:note> increased unto a multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude; and the LORD hath blessed thee <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> at my foot.</ns0:note> since my coming <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>at my foot, i. e.</ns0:hi> upon my coming, since my feet entred into thy house, Or, <ns0:hi>by my foot,</ns0:hi> i. e. by my ministery and labour, as this phrase is used, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 11. 10.</ns0:note>: and now when shall I provide for mine own house also <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">According to my duty, which also is thy interest.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="31">31 And he said, what shall I give thee? and Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me any thing: If thou wilt do this thing for me, I will again feed <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> keep thy flock.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="32">32 I will pass thorow all thy flock to day, re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />moving from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Which may seem to be thus distinguished <ns0:hi>speckled</ns0:hi> with little spots, and <ns0:hi>spotted</ns0:hi> with greater spots or stains, both of divers co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lours from the rest of the body. Or, the <ns0:hi>speckled</ns0:hi> may be the same with the <ns0:hi>ring-streaked,</ns0:hi> by comparing this with <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 35.</ns0:note>: and all the brown <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Or <ns0:hi>black,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>dark-coloured,</ns0:hi> for the Hebrew word signifies also great <ns0:hi>heat</ns0:hi> which produceth such a colour.</ns0:note> cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats; and of <ns0:hi>such</ns0:hi> shall be my hire <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>then shall be my hire; and</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>then,</ns0:hi> as is frequent in Scripture. The sense is, <ns0:hi>Then,</ns0:hi> when the speckled and spotted and brown are separated, and none but white remaining, <ns0:hi>my hire shall be</ns0:hi> out of those white ones, and that in such manner as is expressed in the following verse, all the white young ones shall be thine, and the speckled and spotted and brown which shall be brought forth by those white ones shall be mine.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="33">33 So shall my righteousness answer for me <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">When the cattle shall contrary to their natural and usual course bring forth young ones of a contrary colour to their own, it will hereby be evident that this is the work of God, who hereby pleads my righteous cause against a cruel and unjust master. Or thus, when thou shalt accuse me of doing thee injury, I shall have this manifest and undeniable evidence of my Righteousness or Innocency, that I have no Cattle but of that colour which is by agreement appro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />priated to me.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> to mor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />row.</ns0:note> in time to come; when it shall come for my hire, before thy face <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>When it,</ns0:hi> i. e. my righteousness, <ns0:hi>shall come to</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>upon my reward,</ns0:hi> i. e. when my righteousness shall appear in the very colour of that Cattle which is allotted to me for my re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward or hire, <ns0:hi>before thy face,</ns0:hi> i. e. thou being present and dili<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gently observing whether I have any Cattle of another colour. But the Hebrew word <ns0:hi>Tabo</ns0:hi> is also of the second person, and so the sense seems to be this, <ns0:hi>When thou shalt come upon my hire</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>reward,</ns0:hi> to wit, to observe and see whether I have any other cattel, than what belongs to me. And so these words come in by way of parenthesis, and the following words, <ns0:hi>before my face,</ns0:hi> are to be joyned to the former words, thus, <ns0:hi>so shall my Righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness answer for me in time to come (when thou shalt come upon my hire) before thy face.</ns0:hi> This I prefer before the other, because the phrase of <ns0:hi>coming upon his hire</ns0:hi> seems more properly to agree to a person, than to his Righteousness.</ns0:note>, every one that is not speckled and spotted amongst the goats, and brown amongst the sheep, that shall be counted stollen with me.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="34">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:31" />34 And Laban said, Behold, I would it might be according to thy word <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Laban</ns0:hi> trusted to the course of nature, whereby cattle usu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally bring forth their young of their own colour; and <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ied upon the providence of an Almighty God and his gratious father.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="35">35 And he removed that day the he-goats that were ring-straked <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Which had lines or strakes like bands about them of di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vers colours from the rest of their body.</ns0:note> and spotted, and all the she<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />goats that were speckled and spotted, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> every one that had <ns0:hi>some</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">This word is oft understood in other texts of Scripture, and here it is so neces<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sarily; as appears both from the thing it self, as it is related, and from the phrase; for he saith not <ns0:hi>that was white,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>that <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>ad white in it,</ns0:hi> to wit, mixed with other colours.</ns0:note> white in it, and all the brown amongst the Sheep, and gave <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> into the hand of his sons.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="36">36 And he set three days journey <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Understand it of the journeying or travelling of sheep, not of men.</ns0:note> betwixt himself and Jacob <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Le<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>t either <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> should mingle and exchange the sheep, or the sheep by the contemplation of the diverse co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />loured ones should bring forth others like to them.</ns0:note>: and Jacob fed the rest of La<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bans flocks.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="37">37 And Jacob took him rods <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">By divine appointment, as will appear in the sequel, which is sufficient for <ns0:hi>Iacobs</ns0:hi> justification.</ns0:note> of green po<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plar, and of the hasel, and chesnut-tree <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Either because these trees were next at hand; or because he saw these in the divine visi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on afterwards mentioned, and would exactly follow his pattern.</ns0:note>, and pilled white strakes in them, and made the white appear <ns0:note n="‖" place="bottom">By pilling off the rind which covered it.</ns0:note> which was in the rods.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="38">38 And he set the rods which he had pilled, before the flocks in the gutters in the watering troughs when the flocks came to drink, that they should conceive when they came to drink <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">When by their refreshment and meeting together they were most likely to generate and conceive.</ns0:note>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="39">39 And the flocks conceived <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>were heated,</ns0:hi> i. e, inflamed or excited and disposed to conceive, and this in a more than ordinary manner by the di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine disposal.</ns0:note> before the rods, and brought forth cattle ring-straked, speckled, and spotted <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">This hath some foundation in nature because of the great power of imagination; and there are divers in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stances in many authors both of Women and of Beasts who ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther by the strong fancying, or by the actual and frequent con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />templation of some certain objects have brought forth young ones exactly <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>f the same colour and complexion, as one did an <ns0:hi>Ethiopian,</ns0:hi> &c. But the Providence of God was the principal cause of this effect, without which the productions of that kind would neither have been so many, nor so certain. This poli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cy of <ns0:hi>Iacobs</ns0:hi> could scarcely be excused from deceit and inju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stice, if it were not manifest that it was done by the direction and authority of the sovereign Lord of all estates, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 31. 9, 11, &c. who may take them from one and give them to ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, as it pleaseth him, who also observed <ns0:hi>Labans</ns0:hi> injustice, and gave to <ns0:hi>Iacob</ns0:hi> no more than he abundantly deserved from <ns0:hi>Laban.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="40">40 And Jacob did separate the lambs <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Such as were ring-straked and brown, from the white, as it here follows.</ns0:note>, and set the faces of the flocks toward the ring-straked, and all the brown <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">He caused them to go foremost, and the white to follow them, that by the continued beholding of them in the time of their conjunction they might have their colour more imprinted upon their fancies and thereby convey it to their young ones.</ns0:note> in the flock of Laban: and he put his own flock by themselves; and put them not unto Labans cattle <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Which he did upon the same reason, lest the constant be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />holding of them should make them bring forth the like, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> single coloured ones.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="41">41 And it came to pass, whensoever the stron<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ger cattle did conceive <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">It is known that the cattle in those parts did conceive and bring forth twice in a year, at spring and in Autumn; and it is supposed that the <ns0:hi>stronger</ns0:hi> here mentioned are such as joyned in the spring, and the <ns0:hi>feeble</ns0:hi> they that joyned in Autumn.</ns0:note>, that Jacob laid the rods before the eyes of the cattle in the gutters, that they might conceive among the rods.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="42">42 But when the cattle were feeble, he put <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> not in: so the feebler were Labans, and the stronger Jacobs.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="43">43 And the man increased exceedingly, and had much cattle, and maid-servants, and men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />servants, and camels, and asses.</ns0:p>
